TypeScript Type System - Part 2

January 15, 2024 by Test Author 1 min read

TypeScript Type System

In this second part of our series, we'll explore TypeScript's powerful type system.

Basic Types

TypeScript provides several basic types:

// Primitives
let name: string = "Alice";
let age: number = 30;
let isStudent: boolean = false;

// Arrays
let numbers: number[] = [1, 2, 3];
let names: Array<string> = ["Alice", "Bob"];

// Tuples
let person: [string, number] = ["Alice", 30];

Interfaces

Interfaces define the shape of objects:

interface User {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  email: string;
  age?: number; // Optional property
}

function getUser(id: number): User {
  return {
    id: id,
    name: "Alice",
    email: "alice@example.com"
  };
}

Type Aliases

Type aliases create a new name for a type:

type ID = string | number;
type UserRole = "admin" | "user" | "guest";

interface AdminUser {
  id: ID;
  role: UserRole;
  permissions: string[];
}

Next Steps

In the final part, we'll cover advanced TypeScript features including generics, decorators, and more!
